story.title: Israel Rejects Trump's Gaza Peace Plan, Demands Hamas Disarmament
story.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has announced the rejection of a 15-point peace plan proposed by former US President Donald Trump, stating that Israel will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas is fully disarmed. Netanyahu emphasized that the current proposal is unacceptable in its present form.

timeline_highlights.summary: President Trump has announced a deal for Hamas to completely disarm, which includes the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. However, the implementation of this deal is contingent upon Israel fulfilling its commitments from a previous agreement.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed in the Gaza plan dispute?
explore_lenses.title: The dispute is over sequencing and acceptance
explore_lenses.summary: The 15-point roadmap already paired Hamas disarmament with a phased Israeli withdrawal. Netanyahu’s August 9 rejection makes clear that Israel does not accept the proposed sequencing or its current terms, despite U.S. assertions that an understanding had been reached.

claims.text: The Board of Peace’s May report describes a phased, internationally verified weapons-decommissioning process, matched with steps by Israel and others; it envisages an IDF withdrawal to Gaza’s perimeter contingent on verified progress.
Netanyahu said Israel rejects the 15-point document and that the IDF will not withdraw until Hamas is “genuinely disarmed”; AP reported that Israel and Washington were still discussing Gaza plans.
Trump had said Israel would withdraw as Hamas’s disarmament was completed, a formulation that differs from Netanyahu’s stated condition against any withdrawal before disarmament.

explore_lenses.label: What would implementation require next?
explore_lenses.title: Verification, a security force, and a civilian handover
explore_lenses.summary: The roadmap calls for a linked transition rather than a single withdrawal decision: verified disarmament, an international stabilization force, Palestinian civilian administration, and reconstruction in cleared areas. Its own May status report said negotiations had not been finalized.

claims.text: The roadmap assigns civilian governance and security to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG), while requiring Hamas and other armed factions to cease military, policing, and administrative roles.

It proposes an International Stabilisation Force to act as a buffer, protect humanitarian operations, and support custody of weapons; reconstruction would start in certified decommissioned areas under NCAG authority.

As of May 15, the Board of Peace reported that roadmap talks were not finalized and said the guarantors—Egypt, Qatar, Türkiye, and the United States—were continuing efforts to resolve outstanding obstacles.

Forecast: Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov said the ceasefire and wider transition hinge on disarmament; he warned that failure to resolve the issue leaves Gaza vulnerable to renewed large-scale fighting and stalled reconstruction.

explore_lenses.label: What do Netanyahu, Hamas, and mediators argue?
explore_lenses.title: All cite disarmament, but differ on conditions
explore_lenses.summary: Netanyahu frames complete Hamas disarmament as a precondition for withdrawal. Hamas says it remains committed to the roadmap while seeking pressure on Israel, and Board of Peace officials argue that Hamas could retain a political—not armed—role after a verified transition.

claims.text: Netanyahu’s position is that Israel cannot withdraw while Hamas retains weapons; he publicly rejected the document while saying discussions with the United States continue.
Hamas political bureau member Bassem Naim said Hamas remained committed to the roadmap and expected mediators and the United States to press Netanyahu to adhere to it.

AP reported that Hamas has said it is willing to hand civilian governance to a committee but has sought an interim administration and police force before a technocratic handover; it has also resisted immediate surrender of its arsenal.
Mladenov said Hamas need not disappear as a political movement if it renounces armed activity, describing electoral participation by a disarmed political party as possible.

story_report.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel has rejected Donald Trump’s 15-point Gaza roadmap, insisting that Israeli forces will not withdraw until Hamas is genuinely and fully disarmed. The stance creates an immediate dispute over the sequence of withdrawal and weapons decommissioning, although discussions between Israel and the United States were continuing. The proposal’s broader transition arrangements, including international verification of disarmament, therefore remain unsettled.

sections.heading: Roadmap Sets Phased Gaza Transition
sections.body: A May report by the Board of Peace outlined a phased process for internationally verified weapons decommissioning, paired with steps by Israel and other parties. It envisaged an Israeli military withdrawal to Gaza’s perimeter as verified progress was made. The roadmap assigned civilian administration and security to the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza, while requiring Hamas and other armed factions to end their military, policing and administrative roles.

sections.heading: Hamas and Israel Differ on Terms
sections.body: Netanyahu’s position is that Israel cannot withdraw while Hamas retains weapons. Hamas political bureau member Bassem Naim said the group remained committed to the roadmap and expected mediators and the United States to press Israel to follow it. AP reported that Hamas has expressed willingness to hand civilian governance to a committee, but has sought an interim administration and police force before a technocratic handover and has resisted immediately surrendering its arsenal.

sections.heading: Disarmament Stalemate Risks Renewed Fighting
sections.body: The plan proposes an International Stabilisation Force to buffer Gaza, protect humanitarian operations and support weapons custody, with reconstruction beginning in certified decommissioned areas under NCAG authority. Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov said the ceasefire and wider transition hinge on disarmament, warning that failure to resolve the issue could leave Gaza vulnerable to renewed large-scale fighting and stalled reconstruction.

unresolved.text: The full July 31 version of the proposed roadmap and Israel’s specific written objections were not publicly available in the reviewed sources.
It remains unclear who would verify disarmament, when and where Israeli withdrawals would occur, and on what terms an international stabilization force would deploy.
The sources do not establish whether Hamas accepts complete independently verified disarmament or whether Israel would accept an amended roadmap.
